summary.text: Roy Cooper is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat in North Carolina. A Nash County attorney, he served in the state House and Senate, was state attorney general from 2001 to 2017 and governor from 2017 to 2025. He won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 92.0% of the vote and is campaigning on lowering costs and his record as governor.

paragraphs.text: Cooper was born and raised in Nash County, North Carolina, where he attended public schools and worked summers on the farm; his campaign says his mother was a public-school teacher.
He earned a B.A. from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 1979 and a J.D. from the UNC School of Law in 1982.

Cooper practiced law in Rocky Mount, representing individuals and small businesses, and worked at his family law firm, Fields & Cooper, handling civil suits, personal injury cases and insurance defense.
Gov. Jim Hunt appointed him to the state goals and policy board before he held elected office.

He was elected to the North Carolina House of Representatives in 1986 and served in the State Senate from 1991 to 2001, working in the legislature on teacher pay and law enforcement and on the state's first children's health insurance initiative, according to his campaign.
Cooper was elected attorney general in 2000 and re-elected in 2004, 2008 and 2012.
In April 2007, his office announced that it was dropping all charges against three former Duke lacrosse players, after the local district attorney had recused himself from the case.
Voters elected Cooper governor on November 8, 2016, and re-elected him in 2020, and he left office on January 1, 2025.
His campaign credits him with securing a bipartisan agreement to expand Medicaid, which it says had brought health coverage to more than 650,000 North Carolinians by early 2025.
Cooper announced his Senate candidacy on July 28, 2025, for the seat Sen. Thom Tillis is leaving.
He and his wife Kristin raised three daughters in Rocky Mount, and he has taught Sunday school and tutored students in local public schools.
